description: RTDP (*real-time dynamic programming*) plans when actions have costs and random outcomes, and a goal must be reached at the lowest expected cost (a *stochastic shortest path problem*). It runs *trials*: from the start state, it sets the state's value to the cheapest expected cost over its actions (a *Bellman backup*), takes the cheapest action and samples a successor. With an *admissible* heuristic (one that never overestimates the cost), the values on the states that trials keep visiting converge to the optimum. The crate's `rtdp` stops when every state that the greedy policy reaches has a *residual* (the change that one more backup would make) of at most ε. It is a baseline for comparisons; use `lrtdp` for real problems.

papers.authors: Andrew G. Barto, Steven J. Bradtke, Satinder P. Singh
papers.title: Learning to act using real-time dynamic programming
